Thanks for this — the spec work here is solid. I checked the defaults against `testdata/openapi.yml` myself and they're right: `includeTrip` defaults to false for trip-for-vehicle (line 806) and to true for trip-details, and the `TripParamDefaults` struct expresses that cleanly. The `parseTripParams` refactor is behavior-preserving, and putting `routeReferenceByID` in `reference_utils.go` is the correct home for it per CONTRIBUTING's Code Reuse section. Flagging the shared-helper impact on `trip-details` in the PR description was the right call too.

One blocker before this can land.

**A missing route reference now 404s the entire request.** In `trip_for_vehicle_handler.go`, the new `routeReferenceByID` lookup turns `sql.ErrNoRows` into `sendNotFound`. That lookup is reference enrichment, not the primary resource — the vehicle and the trip were both found successfully by that point, and the trip reference has already been appended to `references.Trips` and is then thrown away. For a feed with a dangling `trips.route_id`, this endpoint stops serving trip details entirely rather than serving them with one route reference absent.

CONTRIBUTING's `ErrNoRows` → 404 rule is about the resource the request names, not about entities you're dereferencing into the references block. The rest of the codebase already treats those differently: `BuildRouteReferences` goes through the batch `GetRoutesByIDs`, where an absent row simply doesn't appear in the result.

The fix is small — on `ErrNoRows`, log and skip the route reference (keeping the trip reference you already built) and let the response go out as a 200. Any other error should still be a 500, which you have right.

Also worth knowing for sequencing: #1279 has landed and #1281 is ahead of you in the queue, both touching this same references block. You'll want to rebase onto `main` once #1281 goes in.

Happy to re-review as soon as the 404 path is sorted.

Reviewed against legacy Java (`TripStatusBeanServiceImpl` / `BeanFactoryV2`, traced directly rather than taken from the wiki) and against `/code-review medium`, CodeRabbit, and SonarQubeCloud findings on this PR.

The core fix is spec-correct and well-tested: the active trip (and now its route) is added to `data.references` whenever a `status` block is built, independent of `includeTrip`, and `trip-for-vehicle`'s `includeTrip` default now correctly matches the spec's documented `false`. Confirmed directly against `TripStatusBeanServiceImpl.getBlockLocationAsStatusBean` and `BeanFactoryV2.getTripStatus`, both of which add the active trip to references with no dependency on `includeTrip`.

Found one correctness bug and two minor cleanup opportunities in the new code — see inline comments.

This PR's own description invokes `trip-for-vehicle.md`'s Extension 4b directly. Tracing that same `includeTrip`/`status` interaction through the Java source (`TripStatusBeanServiceImpl.getBlockLocationAsStatusBean` L294-295, `BeanFactoryV2.getTripStatus` L528-537) shows the sibling `trip-details` endpoint has the identical exemption — the active trip is added to references whenever a `status` block is built, regardless of `includeTrip` — and `trip_details_handler.go`'s existing (unchanged) code already implements it correctly. `trip-details.md`'s Extension 4c didn't document this exemption at all, describing `includeTrip=false` as suppressing the trip record with no carve-out.

No code change is needed here, since `trip_details_handler.go` already behaves correctly — I've corrected the wiki text on our end to match `trip-for-vehicle.md`'s Extension 4b language, so the spec stops contradicting itself across two endpoints backed by the same Java code path. Flagging it here for visibility since it surfaced directly from this PR's own change.

Reviewed the includeTrip/includeStatus fix for trip-for-vehicle. The core fix (active trip + route always added to references when status is present, includeTrip default corrected to false) is spec-consistent and well tested — verified against the legacy Java implementation and confirmed no client impact across Wayfinder, JS SDK, iOS, and Android.

Two things worth addressing before merge, both scoped to this PR's own diff:

1. A correctness gap in the new cross-agency route handling (blocking).

Per CONTRIBUTING.md: "Add new commits when addressing requested changes — don't rewrite already-reviewed history. Rebasing or force-pushing after review has started means the whole PR has to be re-reviewed."
